requirements.note: Participant announcement and registry session rules require manifest before state.
Per-session sequence counters and durable receiver replay floors are enforced.
Envelope source time and state freshness are mandatory and bounded.
Registry freshness and transport replay rejection are tested.
Mode and safety are separate required state fields.
Semantic summaries are bounded to 1,024 UTF-8 bytes.
Robot manifests permit an empty capability tuple.
Capability names require a namespace and version suffix.
Descriptions and valid JSON input/output schemas are required.
Availability has available, busy, degraded, and unavailable values.
Participant validates capability inputs before adapter invocation.
Native adapters return explicit rejection outcomes.
The owner service and CLI support one goal or a bounded unique batch, with every proposal validated before any batch publication.
Planner is a public transport-independent protocol with a trusted replaceable factory contract.
Planner context is limited to goal participants after peer disclosure filtering; the complete authorized awareness-to-outcome path is exercised over mutual TLS.
Every planner proposal passes local validation before publication or dispatch.
Structural, capability, dependency, cycle, time, serialization, and conservative 64 KiB envelope-size validation occurs before journaling or publication.
Independent steps become ready together and an opt-in bounded participant worker pool executes native high-level assignments concurrently with ordered publication.
Dependencies dispatch only after durable successful outcomes.
Failures and unknown work are durable and never blindly retried.
Replanning creates a separately journaled plan with a new ID, exactly incremented revision, explicit predecessor, and immutable prior history.
Any Planner implementation may return a human-authored plan.
Default participant authorization denies every remote assignment.
Leases bind issuer, robot, capabilities, and receiver-local time.
Operational coordinator dispatch requires a target lease identifier.
Lease checks use receiver-local time and fail closed for uncertainty.
Grant, renewal, revocation, expiry, and durable audit are implemented.
Authority mutation is robot-local and absent from the wire protocol.
Authorization precedes journal claim and adapter execution.
Lease approval does not bypass native acceptance or cancellation authority.
The closed message type set contains no actuator commands.
Assignments carry desired high-level capability outcomes and criteria.
Adapters explicitly accept or reject execution and cancellation.

State-only safety streams have independent sequence and durable replay floors, prioritized per-stream queue heads, independent sender locks, concurrent inbox ordering, and reserved capacity without reordering operational sequences.

A bounded watchdog derives required-peer communication loss from semantic-state freshness and edge-triggers manufacturer-defined loss/restoration behavior; callback failures are observable and retried.
The protocol and network profile explicitly reject emergency-stop representation.
Canonical JSON and schema conformance have byte-exact vectors.
Unknown optional envelope fields do not alter known-field decoding.
Unsupported protocol versions fail closed before dispatch.

Shared poses use explicit frames and SI meters; every numeric capability schema field recursively requires a bounded SI-profile unit annotation, and spatial units require a named required string frame property.
Large sensor content is excluded by the core limit and represented by bounded metadata-only absolute URIs with media type, length, SHA-256, observation time, optional expiry, and optional frame.
